closed_issues.title: Rectify information in `cpuload` column and also include custom column `CPU Load (%)`
closed_issues.description:
# Issue

![image](/uploads/2134b7e2be8a4b8df2dcfd6139f93b54/image.png){width="324" height="165"}

The `cpuload` column is currently hard to read because one has to always refer to the `CPU (Tot)` column (_ideally `cpuload` should be equal to `CPU(Tot)`_). There are currently three issues with the `cpuload` column

- Values are not in a fixed range (for e.g. between 0-100), so its hard to compare 1 node to another (_look at image above_)
- Sometimes the value of `cpuload` exceeds that of `CPU (Tot)` column, so users not aware of this issue might get confused (_it essentially means that there are many threads backlogged on those CPUs_)
- Finally, the raw values (from `scontrol`) sometimes do not have the same range too (_look at image below_). So that too needs to be handled.

![image](/uploads/8c278245e5192658fff849e7c3e08c22/image.png){width="316" height="24"}

```
(using " scontrol show node <node-name>")
CPUAlloc=72 CPUEfctv=72 CPUTot=72 CPULoad=64.00

(using " scontrol --json show node <node-name>")
"nodes": [{
   "cpu_load": 6400,
}]
```

# Suggestion

Once the raw values for `cpuload` are properly parsed, then we can display a new custom column called `CPU Load (%)` that shows values between 0-100 % or \>100% if the `cpuload` \> `CPU (Tot)`

closed_issues.title: GPU information is sometimes incorrect so custom/robust regex should be used
closed_issues.description:
# Issue
Currently `cfgtres` and `alloc_tres` in `src/slurm_viewer/data/node_model.py` uses a static regex. That can lead to failures, since this field is custom defined for each cluster. For e.g. 
1. Cluster 1 (_currently works_)
   - 2/3 GPUs allocated and thats what we see in slurm-viewer
   - ![image](/uploads/a4448fec6d25ad3230769195a93e6994/image.png){width=416 height=26}
   - ```
      (using "scontrol show node <node_name>")
      CfgTRES=cpu=16,mem=250G,billing=16,gres/gpu=3 
      AllocTRES=cpu=10,mem=190000M,gres/gpu=2,gres/gpu:rtx6000=2

      (using "scontrol --json show node <node_name>")
      "nodes": [{
      ...,
      "tres": "cpu=16,mem=250G,billing=16,gres\/gpu=3",
      "tres_used": "cpu=10,mem=190000M,gres\/gpu=2,gres\/gpu:rtx6000=2",
      ...
      }]
      ```

2. Cluster 2 (_currently does not work_)
   - 4/4 GPUs allocated, but we dont see that in slurm-viewer
   - ![image](/uploads/3c3ea21aa7bad4603af1e202750c6031/image.png){width=411 height=28}
    - ```
      (using "scontrol show node <node_name>")
      CfgTRES=cpu=72,mem=480G,billing=512,gres/cpu=72,gres/gpu=4,gres/gpu:a100=4
      AllocTRES=cpu=72,mem=468000M,gres/cpu=72,gres/gpu=4,gres/gpu:a100=4

      (using "scontrol --json show node <node_name>")
      "nodes": [{
      ...,
      "tres": "cpu=72,mem=480G,billing=512,gres\/cpu=72,gres\/gpu=4,gres\/gpu:a100=4",
      "tres_used": "cpu=72,mem=468000M,gres\/cpu=72,gres\/gpu=4,gres\/gpu:a100=4",
      ...
      }]
      ```

# Reproduce Issue
Currently `CFGTRESS_RE = r'^cpu=(?P<cpu>\d+),mem=(?P<mem>\d+\w),billing=(?P<billing>\d+),gres/gpu=(?P<gpu>\d+)$'`, so it works on Cluster 1 and not Cluster 2
```python
import re
CFGTRESS_RE = r'^cpu=(?P<cpu>\d+),mem=(?P<mem>\d+\w),billing=(?P<billing>\d+),gres/gpu=(?P<gpu>\d+)$'
m = re.search(CFGTRESS_RE, "cpu=16,mem=250G,billing=16,gres/gpu=3")
m.groupdict() # {'cpu': '16', 'mem': '250G', 'billing': '16', 'gpu': '3'}

m = re.search(CFGTRESS_RE, "cpu=72,mem=480G,billing=512,gres/cpu=72,gres/gpu=4,gres/gpu:a100=4")
m # None
``` 

# Suggestions
1. Allow for custom regex
2. Build a more robust regex
```python
# Option 1
extract_params = lambda s: {match[0]: match[1] for match in re.findall(r'(\w+\/\w+|\w+)=([\w\d]+)', s)}

string1 = "cpu=16,mem=250G,billing=16,gres/gpu=3"
extract_params(string1) # {'cpu': '16', 'mem': '250G', 'billing': '16', 'gres/gpu': '3'}

string2 = "cpu=72,mem=480G,billing=512,gres/cpu=72,gres/gpu=4,gres/gpu:a100=4"
extract_params(string2) # {'cpu': '72', 'mem': '480G', 'billing': '512', 'gres/cpu': '72', 'gres/gpu': '4', 'a100': '4'}
```

```python
# Option 2
extract_params = lambda s: {match[0].split('/')[-1]: match[1] for match in re.findall(r'(\w+\/\w+|\w+)=([\w\d]+)', s) if match[0].split('/')[-1] in {'cpu', 'mem', 'billing', 'gpu'}}

string1 = "cpu=16,mem=250G,billing=16,gres/gpu=3"
extract_params(string1) # {'cpu': '16', 'mem': '250G', 'billing': '16', 'gpu': '3'}

string2 = "cpu=72,mem=480G,billing=512,gres/cpu=72,gres/gpu=4,gres/gpu:a100=4"
extract_params(string2) # {'cpu': '72', 'mem': '480G', 'billing': '512', 'gpu': '4'}
```

closed_issues.title: Only show those partitions that user has access to (by default)
closed_issues.description:
When I first open up slurm-viewer, it shows me information for all partitions on the SLURM cluster. This has two issues
 - its an information overload (if a cluster has too many partitions)
 - user needs to spend time selecting the relevant partitions (every time), or they have to go and change the `~/.config/slurm-viewer/settings.toml` file.

The `scontrol` command (_that gathers information for the Nodes tab_) only shows those partitions for which the user has access to (_unless appended by  `--all`_). So we can use that limited information for `scontrol` to our advantage (_in `src/slurm_viewer/data/slurm_communication.py`_) and show only partitions that user has access to.
